articles.title: Building desktop software for a network that never touches the internet
articles.excerpt: Most advice for building software assumes a server somewhere. Kote has none. It is an armoury and asset custody system in use by a unit of the Pakistan Army, and the PCs it runs on sit on a closed net…
articles.body: Most advice for building software assumes a server somewhere. Kote has none. It is an armoury and asset custody system in use by a unit of the Pakistan Army, and the PCs it runs on sit on a closed network or no network at all. Some of them are old enough that 32-bit Windows is a supported target. There is no IT team to run a database and no internet to fetch an update. The job sounds simple: know at any moment which weapon or ammunition lot is where, and who holds it. The constraints are what make it hard. Here are the decisions they forced, with the real code. The shape of the app One PC, no network, four layers. It is one Electron program per office PC. React draws the UI, SQLite (through better-sqlite3 ) holds the data, and the two only talk through a narrow, typed bridge.
articles.author: Ahmad Dogar

articles.title: Don't let the model do the math: how to build AI reports people can check
articles.excerpt: An analyst in a trucking control tower built their dashboards with AI, and they still recheck every one of them in Python. In an r/ChatGPT thread from 2 November 2026 they explained why: if their boss…
articles.body: An analyst in a trucking control tower built their dashboards with AI, and they still recheck every one of them in Python. In an r/ChatGPT thread from 2 November 2026 they explained why: if their bosses find a single inconsistency in the data, the analyst is the one in trouble. The top reply had 19 votes. It said, in short: stop asking the model to do the math, and ask it to write the code that does the math. That is one thread from one person. It is not a measured trend. We think it gets the design decision right anyway. The answer In our view, users don't distrust AI analysis because the model is dumb. They distrust it because the model is doing the arithmetic, and nothing on the screen says where a number came from. So split the job. Code computes every figure.
articles.author: iloblique

articles.title: GPU-as-a-service vs buying your own hardware: a real cost comparison for Indian startups
articles.excerpt: A GPU on your balance sheet feels like an asset. A GPU on your invoice feels like a cost. For most Indian startups, the numbers say the invoice is the cheaper way to hold it. What does GPU as a servic…
articles.body: A GPU on your balance sheet feels like an asset. A GPU on your invoice feels like a cost. For most Indian startups, the numbers say the invoice is the cheaper way to hold it. But "most" is not "all," and the break-even point is more specific than the usual rent-versus-buy slogans admit. Here are real 2026 Indian price points, a three-year comparison you can rerun with your own numbers, and the conditions under which buying does win. What does GPU as a service mean, and what is the alternative? GPU as a service simply means renting GPU time from a provider, by the hour or by the month, instead of owning the hardware. The alternative is buying the card or server yourself and running it in your own space or in a colocation facility.

articles.title: Why does your Galaxy restart several times during a firmware update?
articles.excerpt: Why does your Galaxy restart several times during a firmware update? You tap install on a software update, the phone restarts, the Samsung logo appears, and then it restarts again. Sometimes it restar…
articles.body: Why does your Galaxy restart several times during a firmware update? You tap install on a software update, the phone restarts, the Samsung logo appears, and then it restarts again. Sometimes it restarts a third time before you ever see your home screen. If you have never watched an update closely, that can feel like something is going wrong. In most cases it is not. The restarts are how Android installs an update, and each one has a job to do. The restarts are part of the update, not a problem A firmware update does not change your phone in one step. It replaces system files while the phone is running, then it needs a clean start so the new files can load instead of the old ones. That first restart is the phone switching over to the new version.

articles.body: Reading about incident response is not the same as doing it at 2:40 left on the clock with three alerts firing. That's why SteadfastIQ now includes Hack the Globe , a live-fire range with 52 levels: 26 for the red team and 26 for the blue team. How it plays Pick a side. Red runs an authorized penetration test against a fictional logistics company. Blue works its SOC: triage, contain, hunt and recover. Every level is a mission. You get a codename briefing, a countdown, a terminal, a network map, alerts and logs. Tap a move or type it. Rewards on both sides. XP, stars, streaks, loot crates, gear every few levels and badges. articles.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy separates browsing contexts, not user accounts
articles.excerpt: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy separates browsing contexts, not user accounts A page can open a cross-origin window and retain an opener relationship. That relationship allows limited access to the new br…
articles.body: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy separates browsing contexts, not user accounts A page can open a cross-origin window and retain an opener relationship. That relationship allows limited access to the new browsing context and can expose navigation behavior that a security team did not intend. The Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy response header lets a document request a different opener policy. It is useful isolation, but it does not authenticate users or protect data after an attacker reaches the same origin. The HTML Standard defines three main values. unsafe-none is the current default and keeps the new document in the same top-level browsing context as its predecessor unless another policy applies.

articles.body: I run a handful of launch boards for indie products. Every morning I used to open analytics and look at the same thing: which sources sent the most visitors. Direct, then Google, then a long tail of small sites. Yesterday I sorted the same table by revenue instead. On EarlyHunt, one referrer I had never paid attention to sent 28 visitors and $69.60 . Google sent 219 visitors and $29.00 over the same window. That's a tiny sample, and I'll get to why I'm not acting on it yet. But the sort order is the point. Sorting by visitors had hidden that row completely. The setup My sites use Minilytics , an open-source analytics tool that runs on a Cloudflare Worker and records payments next to visits.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.body: On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.

articles.title: Relive Starship’s historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and ‘Mechazilla’ tower catch
articles.excerpt: See the most epic photos from SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 test flight and historic launch tower catch.
articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.

articles.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX’s Starship, already the largest rocket on Earth, will get even bigger with next-gen V4 model
articles.excerpt: Just a day after SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket back at the launch pad for the first time ever, Elon Musk told us that the spacecraft will get even bigger.
articles.body: As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big. The company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower. It was a huge moment for SpaceX , bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship. "Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15).
